title: Dispatch: dying and death saves for encounter combatants (attempt 1)
description:
Implements capability bead eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.5 (read `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.5`). Integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 (single PR for eight beads). Your branch already contains eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4 (character suffocation gate: migration 0032 character.recovery_block, hpLifecycle beginSuffocation/endSuffocation, tool set_suffocation) — read that code first and mirror it. Read AGENTS.md; docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendment A5; ADR 0020 §§2-3.

SOURCE: SRD rule:monsters-and-death: "Most GMs have a monster die the instant it drops to 0 hit points, rather than having it fall unconscious and make death saving throws. Mighty villains and special nonplayer characters are common exceptions; the GM might have them fall unconscious and follow the same rules as player characters." SRD rule:suffocating makes any creature "drop to 0 hit points and [be] dying, and it can't regain hit points or be stabilized until it can breathe again." The character death rules live in packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts (header comment lists them).

DESIGN (decided by the supervisor; implement exactly):
1. Migration packages/core/data/migrations/0033_combatant_death_rules.sql (next contiguous number). SQLite cannot alter a CHECK, so rebuild encounter_combatant per the ADR 0015 conventions already used in this repo (find a prior table-rebuild migration and copy its pattern, preserving every column, index, and trigger): status CHECK gains 'dying' and 'stable'; new columns death_rules TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'monster' CHECK IN ('monster','player-character'); death_save_successes / death_save_failures INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK BETWEEN 0 AND 3; recovery_block TEXT CHECK (NULL or 'suffocating'); stable recovery columns mirroring character 0020 (stable_recovery_roll 1..4, anchor/deadline elapsed minutes). If campaign_actor's status CHECK (0001) is synced from combatant status in updateCombatant, extend it the same way in this migration (dying/stable) or map them explicitly in the sync — choose extending the CHECK so actor state is not lossy. Regenerate the schema snapshot with `npm run -w @eshyra/core schema:snapshot`. Update schema.ts column-semantics comments.
2. Default behaviour is unchanged: a 'monster' combatant reaching 0 HP is dead unless another status is passed.
3. update_combatant gains `deathRules?: 'player-character'` (one-way opt-in per combatant; once set it persists for that combatant) and `critical?: boolean` (meaning as adjust_hp's: damage at 0 HP from a critical hit). For a 'player-character' combatant the engine applies the character death rules: hpDelta bringing it to 0 → 'dying' with counters reset, or 'dead' when the overflow beyond 0 (|hpDelta| - previous hp) is >= hpMax (instant death); damage while dying/stable at 0 → one death-save failure (two if critical), stable → dying, three failures → dead; healing from 0 → 'alive', counters reset (refused while recovery_block is set). Combatants have no temporary HP column today: do not invent one. Factor the shared transition logic out of hpLifecycle.ts into a pure function both paths call, rather than duplicating rules.
4. Death saves and stabilization for combatants: record_death_save and stabilize_character accept an optional `combatantId` (mutually exclusive with `character`; error if both). Same outcome rules as characters, including the suffocation block semantics from 0032 (nat 20 = one success no HP while blocked; third success does not stabilize while blocked). Only a 'player-character' combatant that is dying may make death saves / be stabilized. Stabilizing arms the 1d4-hour recovery deadline exactly as for characters (seeded rng), and the existing world-clock resolution path (resolveStableRecoveries, called from rest.ts and the clock advance path — find every caller) also resolves due combatant recoveries (regain 1 HP → alive). A combatant whose combat instance is closed keeps its state; resolve recoveries regardless of instance status, and sync to the campaign actor when identity_kind is campaign_actor (as updateCombatant does).
5. Suffocation for combatants: set_suffocation accepts `combatantId` (mutually exclusive with character). event 'drop' on a combatant: sets hp 0 and recovery_block; status 'dying' for a 'player-character' combatant; for a 'monster' combatant the rule is applied under rule:monsters-and-death's default — status 'dead' — and the result says so (the DM opts the creature into 'player-character' first if it should be dying). 'breathe' clears the block (and stabilizes on 3 accrued successes, as for characters).
6. Concentration (F3): dying and stable are incapacitated/down; extend the wasDown/isDown logic in updateCombatantInTxn and anywhere else that enumerates CombatantStatus (grep the whole src tree for each status literal and for CombatantStatus / COMBATANT_STATUSES / ActorStatus) — action economy gates (actionEconomy.ts: a dying/stable participant cannot act; only death was hard-gated, so add dying/stable alongside the existing incapacitation handling only if the module already gates unconscious; otherwise leave it), context assembly / roster rendering (render death-save counters like formatHpStatus does for characters), close_combat_instance, start_encounter.
7. Tool descriptions: update_combatant (remove "combatants have no dying or death-save state"; state the deathRules opt-in, the 0-HP behaviour for each, critical), record_death_save, stabilize_character, set_suffocation — contracts only, no per-rule prose, no arithmetic recipes.
8. Known limits (ruleKnownLimits.ts), R0 re-derivation: rule:suffocating's combatant sentence becomes the bounded path (combatant: opt into player-character death rules with update_combatant deathRules, then set_suffocation drop/breathe); remove 'combatant-dying-state' from its capabilityGaps and from ENGINE_CAPABILITY_GAPS. If rule:suffocating then carries no gap at all, delete the capabilityGaps field for it. Participants must list every tool named in the statement and appear in it. Update the identity-pinned gapsByKey map in packages/core/test/rules/ruleAwareness.test.ts and the suffocation assertions there and in tools.test.ts (replace the old "no dying status" assertions with assertions on the new contract; the 8-word source-restatement test must stay green). Design doc A5 table: note the combatant-dying-state gap as landed in eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.5.

TESTS (generalized, through real tool invocation where the contract is model-facing): monster default unchanged (0 HP → dead; explicit status still wins); player-character: drop to 0 → dying; overflow instant death; damage at 0 → failures (+critical); three failures dead; heal from 0 → alive; death saves incl. nat 1 / nat 20 / three successes; stabilize + recovery deadline resolved by the clock path; suffocation drop/breathe for both death-rule modes incl. blocked healing and blocked stabilization; concentration broken on dying; actor sync of the new statuses; migration preserves existing rows (follow the migration test patterns in migrationRunner/migrationLegacyAdoption tests).

OUT OF SCOPE: combatant temporary HP; nonlethal knockout (separate bead); anything not listed.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation per the description on its own branch; npm run verify:worktree green before commit; completion report in bd notes; bead closed by the child.
